data.headline: CIO / CTO Technology Leader - Applied Innovation and Impact Engineering Leadership
data.about:
With over 30 years of experience delivering technology solutions across every scale — from startups to global enterprises — I’ve progressed from graduate software engineering intern through engineering leadership, technical and enterprise architecture, to CxO-level strategy and delivery. At every step, I’ve remained grounded in hands-on execution while developing the ability to craft and deliver strategic technology vision that aligns with business goals and unlocks meaningful change.

Today, I focus on helping organisations navigate the paradigm shift toward AI-infused business models and AI-augmented technology delivery, with a particular emphasis on reimagining the software development lifecycle (SDLC) for this next chapter.

Having led both change and run functions across multiple sectors, I bring a balanced perspective on transformation: understanding the importance of stability and operational excellence while delivering bold, future-facing innovation. I’ve architected and implemented solutions across platforms ranging from embedded and mainframe to cloud-native, decentralised, and Web3 — always with an eye on long-term value and organisational readiness.

My core value is my ability to operate fluently at every level — from executive strategy to technical execution — and to align diverse teams around shared intent. I create momentum in complexity, favour team dynamics over rigid structure, and get real satisfaction from building high-performing environments where people thrive amid uncertainty.

I’m genuinely optimistic about the opportunities AI brings. While it challenges us to adapt, it also reminds us of the timeless value of brilliant basics: clarity of thought, purposeful execution, and continuous learning.

subComponents.title: Director of Engineering, Aviva Digital Platforms
subComponents.caption: Jun 2023 - Aug 2024 · 1 yr 2 mos

description.text: Working as a technology strategy consultant supporting C-suite executives in numerous large scale Enterprises i provided direction and execution oversight in a range of engagements from trouble-shooting failing digital transformation programs, establishing strategic data-archtiecture and within an enterprise growing inorganically, and bringing significant domain expertise from cloud engineering, enteprise security and GDPR regulatory controls.

Reporting into the Plusnet CEO with a line into BT Consumer CIO, I was responsible for all platform delivery and operations, covering enterprise, e-commerce, service delivery, CRM, and ERP/supply-chain systems. My organisation spanned 3 UK sites with an engineering centre established in Bangalore, circa 250 staff within an annualised run-the-business budget of circa £10m. Operationally I was responsible for the platforms underpinning a 24x7 business operation of around 1000 call-centre, front-line and business operations staff, and the end-to-end UK broadband network platform running residential and business services to a base of circa 1 million UK customers. 

Key achievements:
- During my time in Plusnet spanning CIO and Chief Architect roles I have underpinned revenue growth of in the region of 300% and scaling of core IT/network platforms to cater for circa 400% customer growth.
- Co-architected a new ground-up portfolio planning and delivery model across numerous demands sources along with technical and operational capacity planning models.
-Delivered online and CRM capabilities to support consistently best-in-industry customer experience (Net Promoter) ratings, whilst addressing numerous major organisational scaling and transformation challenges. 
- Delivered a new strategic core broadband network with significant cost efficiencies
- Increased overall software pipeline efficiency/productivity by circa 30% through targeted organisational and delivery model change across the software-delivery-life-cycle. 
-Established a tighter operational culture around critical services and delivered significantly improved annualised platform availability results.

Reporting into the COO/CIO, I was responsible for technical strategy and long term evolution of network and IT platforms whilst achieving cost-effective sustainable growth into a large scale, regulated enterprise entering next-generation markets. 
Key achievements included:
- Formation of an applied Enterprise Architecture function and establishing platform roadmaps to facilitate extension of the business/IT planning horizon.
- Stabilization and scaling of core business processes and IT capabilities addressing a range of growth related scaling challenges.
- Establish SOA and capability based architecture blueprint for OSS/BSS roadmaps with associated clarification of business function and process context within a hugely diverse organic software ecosystem.
- Deliver next generation services such as Over-the-top (OTT) TV, and real-time traffic policy control within the UK broadband network context, taking Plusnet into the triple-play market.

subComponents.title: CIT Transformation Architect, BT Global Platforms
subComponents.caption: Feb 2009 - May 2010 · 1 yr 3 mos

description.text:
Responsible for delivering an optimised end-to-end delivery model for the BT Consumer IT delivery organisation to achieve reduced defect rates and increase product quality. I designed an innovative enterprise-scale Continuous Integration Testing (CIT) facet of the newly established BT Enterprise Operating Model and put it to work across the BT Consumer business and the BT TSO delivery organisation. The goal was to reduce the level of defects entering formal QA phase of the combined stack delivery program after weeks of parallel development spanning many teams and significant investment. This program led to circa 80% p1/p2 defect reduction in handover to formal QA phase and was a resounding success.
Key achievements include:
- defined the revised end-to-end delivery process (CIT) as an extension of traditional waterfall delivery model.
- engaged with over 30 component delivery organisations (circa 1500 person organisation) to engage and refine the CIT approach.
- assembled a federated test environment and support organisation avoiding capital investment within the program.
- worked with component delivery managers to cultivate an interlocking approach to cross-platform sprint-planning and commitments to key points of integration testing within the delivery sprints. 
- formed a CIT automation team who proactively and continuously verified key integration and functional risks during the development phase of the project.
- developed a range of innovative middleware tools to support pre-emptive identification of integration risk, and radically reduce the diagnosis timeframe for common integration problems.

Based on the success of my previous role I gained the opportunity to broaden my field and apply my integration specialisation to a range of front-line business problems, where different variations of technology and patterns were required to increase flexibility and cost control options. During this time, I worked with a small group of specialists, applying the architecture of the web, characterised by REST architectural style across a range of internal systems and capabilities with the goal of establishing an alternative implementation architecture for enterprise patterns at lower cost. Where portfolio commercial middleware technologies were incompatible with programs implementing packaged and/or disposable API’s I was responsible for mapping key interaction patterns across multiple technologies including open-source and lightweight alternative frameworks. The output of this series of engagements was an acceleration of adoption of BT’s platform maturity model, in which integration API’s and SDK’s were manufactured far more efficiently and with reduced full-life cost through selective avoidance of commercial ‘heavy’ technology.

At the formation of BT’s redefined strategic architecture I had the role of Integration Platform Architect within the wider community of enterprise architects. My role was to define the platform, capabilities and roadmap associated with shaping how functional platforms communicated across domain boundaries effectively. I worked extensively on defining a logical and technical blue-print for platform API and capability-based integration, techniques for managing and integrating common, exchange and localised data-models, and increasing the precision and consistency of engineering integration at a scale. Key components of this architecture are still evident today across all BT lines of business, a testament to its enduring success. During this time, I became a recognized authority on implementation architecture for SOA, EAI, ESB, and RESTful styles of enterprise integration. More progressive aspects of this role were involvement in BT’s initial API strategy, and a research program I initiated in which emerging semantic web and graph-database technologies could be exploited to reduce full-life-cost of such enterprise web-services and RESTful integration architectures. The experiences and skills I gained in this role cut across industry vertical (TOGAF/ISEB architectural frameworks) and are directly applicable to all EA contexts.

Responsible for technical direction for a newly formed EAI function within a broader 'SOE' business transformation program in BT Global Services core OSS/BSS. This established a standard engagement model across all functional areas in specifying, delivering and exploiting centralised EAI capabilities as functional IT platforms were introduced, retired and decommissioned in each iteration of the program.

Responsible for the team management and technical direction for the systems team (15+ engineers) delivering the operational platforms for the 24x7 management of a national network of 250K traditional pay-phones and next-gen broadband enabled multimedia terminals – the first public touchscreen online terminal estate in the UK.
